## Headline

The procedure is in notes/procedure.md. The procedure fixed all three notes files, and each file now passes check_file.

- notes/a.md had one banned word ("clearly"). The word is removed.
- notes/b.md had one long sentence. It is now four short sentences.
- notes/c.md had one banned word ("very") and one long sentence. Both are fixed.

## Background

The request asked for a numbered procedure to fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file. It then asked to apply the procedure to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md in order. The meaning of each file had to stay the same.

## Relevance

The three notes now meet the style limits, so the team can reuse them. Any agent can reuse the procedure on new notes files.

## Information

Evidence from the check_file tool, run in this session [1]:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| notes/a.md | 1 banned word, 0 long sentences | 0 and 0 |
| notes/b.md | 0 banned words, 1 long sentence | 0 and 0 |
| notes/c.md | 1 banned word, 1 long sentence | 0 and 0 |

Meaning check [judgment]: I did not add or remove any fact. I only deleted the boosters and split the long sentences. For example, the note in b.md still says the cache filled, the service used the database, and this lasted until the import ended.

Assumption log:

Assumption: the check_file tool reports all banned words. Why not measured: no tool can reach the full banned list. Validate by: read each file once more. If wrong: more edits are needed.

Alternative considered: rewrite each file from scratch. This loses because it risks a change of meaning, and small edits keep the original wording [judgment].

## End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard for note edits. Increment: add it to the team's notes folder (done). Blocker removed: no shared edit method. Test (deterministic): Given a notes file with a banned word, When an agent follows the procedure, Then check_file reports zero problems. Cynefin: Clear, because the rule is known and deduction from the checker applies.
2. Run check_file on every new notes file before it is shared. Increment: one file per session. Blocker removed: style errors reach readers. Test (deterministic): Given a new file, When check_file runs, Then it reports no failures. Cynefin: Clear, because the checker gives a fixed answer.
3. Review the meaning of edited files by a human reader. Increment: the three files above. Blocker removed: the tool cannot check meaning. Test (evaluative): rubric with criteria "facts kept" (weight 70%) and "clear wording" (weight 30%), pass threshold 90%, evidence is a side-by-side read of old and new text. Cynefin: Complicated, because expert analysis of the text picks the answer by deduction.

Step 3 MUST NOT start until the test in Step 1 passes.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

Use this procedure on one file at a time. Replace PATH with the file path.

1. Call list_files. Confirm that PATH exists.
2. Call read_file on PATH. Keep the original text in your context.
3. Call check_file on PATH. Note each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
4. Write the new text. Replace each banned word with a plain word or delete it. Keep the facts the same.
5. Split each long sentence into two or more short sentences. Keep each sentence under 20 words. Do not drop any fact.
6. Keep the headings, lists, and order of the original.
7. Call write_file on PATH with the full new text. This replaces the old content.
8. Call check_file on PATH again. If it reports any banned word or long sentence, go to Step 4.
9. Compare the new text with the original from Step 2. Confirm that the meaning is the same.
10. Go to the next file only when Step 8 reports zero problems.
